claims.text: The as-deposited Fe25Ni21Mn24Si13Ge17 films and nanoribbon arrays are amorphous.
The as-deposited material has a single cubic-type short-range order and no long-range crystalline order.
The as-deposited material has smooth surfaces.
Annealing at 700 K promotes short-range atomic reordering in the amorphous alloy.
Annealing at 700 K relaxes residual fabrication-induced strain.
Annealing-induced reordering and strain relaxation reduce local domain-pinning barriers.
Annealing-induced short-range reordering improves collective ferromagnetic exchange interactions.
Improved collective exchange increases the effective ferromagnetic volume fraction.
The increased effective ferromagnetic fraction enhances magnetization and spin-entropy variation.
Ribbon spacing dictates the degree of inter-ribbon magnetic coupling.
Applied elastic longitudinal strain up to 2% generates residual magnetoelastic anisotropy.
Strain-induced magnetoelastic coupling stabilizes magnetic order against thermal fluctuations above 100 K.
Elastic longitudinal strain up to 2% does not alter the blocking-peak position.
Elastic longitudinal strain up to 2% preserves film isotropy.
The unannealed baseline has an isothermal magnetic entropy change of approximately 1.25 J kg−1 K−1 at 140 K for a 50 kOe field change.
Annealing 1 µm-spaced nanoribbons at 700 K increases magnetization relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing at 700 K enhances the conventional isothermal magnetic entropy change over roughly 40–200 K.
Annealing at 700 K does not induce bulk crystallization or compromise mechanical stability.
Annealing near 1000 K can induce bulk crystallization and lies outside the proposed pre-crystallization regime.

contradictions.description: Applied strain is said to generate residual magnetoelastic anisotropy while also leaving film isotropy unchanged. These statements are inconsistent unless the type or direction of anisotropy is distinguished explicitly.
